evidence.quote: But there is an important risk with today's low sensitivity of inflation to slack: It makes it more difficult to boost inflation to our objective of 2 percent on a sustainable basis.
And the unemployment rate is at a 50-year low.
But when equilibrium interest rates are low, we have less room to cut interest rates and thus less room to buffer the economy using our conventional tool.

The Federal Reserve could hold interest rates lower after a recession is over, perhaps by promising not to raise interest rates until inflation or the unemployment rate have reached a particular level.
Last year, core inflation was very close to our goal.

parsed.rationale: This framework-review speech emphasizes the risk of persistently low inflation and limited policy space, and it discusses make-up and yield-target strategies that would keep rates lower for longer. It gives no near-term rate signal, so the dovish lean is mild and structural.
